Ethan / Kimberly —

Attached: 2026-09-26_pinelab_usage_report_q3.csv and pine-street_roster_ma_plan_v2.pdf

Highlights (Q2→Q3):
- Average daily tokens: 2.1M → 2.56M (22% increase)
- Peak daily tokens (95th percentile): 3.8M
- Commit utilization (30‑day rolling): 72% average, 92% at peak surge windows
- Latency (prod, v1): median 120ms, p95 430ms; after int8 quantization p95 reduced to ~370ms
- Cost impact: effective per‑M token spend down from $16.8 to $14.8 (~12% savings)

Recommended short‑term bridge for Nov launch (6 weeks):
1) Add a 20% commit increase for Q4 ramp (est. incremental commit cost: $18,200/mo).
2) Provision 2x burst credit pool (~500K tokens/day capacity) to absorb traffic spikes.
3) Enable automatic fallback routing to a slightly lower‑capacity model variant for non‑critical flows (saves ~25% CPU/GPU cycles when invoked).

Fallback / risk mitigations:
- If burst utilization >70% for 48 hours, automatic alert to PineStreet on-call + option to convert burst to temporary Dedicated capacity.
- Recommend retention of current int8 quantization and enable prefix caching for heavy conversational flows (estimated additional 8–10% token savings).

Next steps: confirm the 20% commit increase and sign the short addendum; Karthik will prepare an addendum template and a two‑week rollback window. Happy to walk through on today's call.

—Monica Patel
Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
